Help

How Summit HQ Works

Everything someone new would need to run the summits from here: what each part does, how it connects to the other systems, and what to do when something goes wrong.

Summit HQ is the MISMO team’s one place to plan each Summit. It holds the task list and deadlines, the week’s schedule room by room, what the hotel sets up, the hotel resume, every speaker and sponsor and where they are in the process, Tuesday’s General Sessions, and the weekly registration numbers.

Open it at resources.mismo.org/summit-hq and sign in with your MISMO resources account. Everything saves on its own as you work, and anyone else who has it open sees your changes within about 30 seconds. A panel that opens on the right has a Save button at the bottom too. New here? Start with Your Part, Person by Person below.

01If You Are Picking This Up

Do these in your first week, in this order. They keep everything running while you learn the rest.

  1. Get access. You need a MISMO resources account with Summit HQ and Sponsorship Portal access (Perry sets these up), and access to the GitMISMO organization on GitHub.
  2. Download a backup. Press Backup at the foot of the left menu and choose Download. Save the file somewhere the team can reach, such as the MISMO Summits SharePoint site.
  3. Take over the automatic emails. The Power Automate flows listed under Emails That Send on Their Own run under Jonna’s Microsoft account. If that account is closed they stop. Ask IT to add you as a co-owner of each flow (or make you the primary owner), then check each one still runs.
  4. Check the old speaker email is off. Bernie now gets one New Speakers to Register list each weekday morning, straight from People. The older flow MISMO Summit HQ - Heads Up for Bernie emailed him one speaker at a time from the Summit HQ People list in Jonna’s OneDrive; it is no longer needed and should be turned off, and that list is no longer used.
  5. Hand over Jonna’s tasks. Open Run of Show, then All Tasks, and give each of Jonna’s open tasks a new owner.
  6. Check the Sponsorship Portal stamp at the foot of the left menu. It should say 0 new changes. If it has said there are changes waiting for more than a day, see When Something Goes Wrong.
02Your Part, Person by Person

Pick your name to see the pages you work in, what you do in them step by step, and the emails Summit HQ sends you. It opens on your own name when you are signed in.

Jonna CritchleyDirector of Programs & Operations. Owns Summit HQ, the schedule, the agenda, General Sessions and the automatic emails.
Your pages

What You Do

  1. Each week, start on Run of Show. Next Up and anything in red come first; mark what needs talking through Need to Discuss so it lands in the Planning Meeting.
  2. Build the week on the Schedule. Drag sessions into rooms, use Arrangement Options for a clean week, and follow the Schedule Timeline for the Chair Survey and the finalized grid.
  3. Build Tuesday on General Sessions: the running order, who is on each segment and who sponsors it.
  4. Add speakers on People. Each one you add goes on Bernie’s next morning list to register on its own.
  5. Ask the MISMO team for their travel dates from MISMO Team at the Summit on People: press Ask for Travel Dates, check the email and send it, and when the dates are in, check who goes to Bernie and press Send to Bernie.
  6. Watch Ready for the Hotel on Hotel Specs and the readiness on the Resume, and issue each new resume version from Versions & Changes.
  7. Review the trunk when Bernie sends it: open the link in the email and press Looks Good or Needs a Change.
  8. Keep this Help page current whenever the way of working changes.

Emails You Get

  • New Speakers to Register (copied) · Board Members to Register (copied) · Tasks Due This Week · sponsorship paid notices and payment follow-ups · The Trunk Is Ready for Review.
Amy MosesVP of Strategic Growth. Places speakers on their General Sessions segments and Workshop sections, and gets every speaker’s bio and headshot in.
Your pages

What You Do

  1. Open People. The Confirmed Speakers wall shows every speaker ringed by how far along they are, with their next step under their name.
  2. Send the speaker email. On the Speaker Emails & Follow-Ups card on People, press Choose Speakers to Email and tick who gets it, or open one speaker and press Send Speaker Email. It carries the hotel booking link and rate from the Resume and each speaker’s own link to send their bio and headshot, and it ticks Asked for bio & headshot for you.
  3. Their bio and headshot come in on their own. When a speaker sends the form, the bio, title, company and headshot land on their row and Bio & headshot in hand ticks itself. Anyone who has not sent theirs gets a reminder every week on the day their email went, until it is in; see Speaker Emails & Follow-Ups on People to see who is next, or to switch the reminders off for someone. You can still type a bio or add a headshot on the speaker’s record yourself.
  4. Build the Workshop on the Workshop page: add sections and drag speakers onto them from your Confirmed Speakers.
  5. See who still owes you something on People: the Need Something From Us box at the top.
  6. Review the trunk when Bernie sends it: open the link in the email and press Looks Good or Needs a Change.

Emails You Get

  • New Speakers to Register (copied) · Tasks Due This Week · sponsorship paid notices and payment follow-ups · The Trunk Is Ready for Review.
Kelly BradshawDirector of Strategic Growth. Sponsors, marketing pieces and the awards ceremony.
Your pages

What You Do

  1. Check sponsors on People. Approved sponsors arrive from the Sponsorship Portal on their own, with their level, what they sponsor and their comp code. They go on the website agenda by themselves (breakfasts, breaks and receptions included), so there is nothing to mark.
  2. Watch the numbers on Registration: this week against last year, and who has registered.
  3. The weekly registration list to sponsors goes out as you (Send As) every Friday at noon Eastern from week 7, the Friday seven weeks before the Friday ahead of the Summit, through the Friday before it; nothing to press.
  4. Review the trunk when Bernie sends it: open the link in the email and press Looks Good or Needs a Change.

Emails You Get

  • New Speakers to Register (copied) · Tasks Due This Week · sponsorship paid notices and payment follow-ups · The Trunk Is Ready for Review.
Bernardo (Bernie) JordanRegisters speakers, the Board and the MISMO team; sends sponsorship invoices; keeps the Trunk.
Your pages

Registering People

  1. Every weekday morning the New Speakers to Register email lists the speakers added since the last one, with their sessions. Register each one.
  2. Mark them registered on People: open the speaker and tick Registered for the event. Anyone registered before the email goes drops off the next list.
  3. The Board: when someone presses Notify Bernie, the Board Members to Register email lists who is still to register. Register them, then press Registered on their row on the Board of Directors card.
  4. The MISMO team: the MISMO Team to Register email lists everyone going under the MISMO banner, with their arrival and departure dates.
  5. Sponsors are never registered by you; they use their comp code. You get each sponsorship invoice to send when the portal approves it.

Packing the Trunk

  1. Open The Trunk. The road across the top shows your Packing List task and its due date, the Team Review, and the day the trunk ships.
  2. Update the list on the left: the − and + buttons change how many, and you can type over any name or note. Add anything new with Add something to pack at the bottom. For Sponsor Merch, press Bring In This Summit’s Sponsors.
  3. Pack each line by dragging it into the trunk, or press its Pack button. On a phone, press and hold a line, then drag. To change or take out something already packed, press it in the trunk.
  4. Send for Review when you are ready. Pick who reviews it (Jonna, Amy and Kelly to start), add a note if you like, and send. The team gets an email with the list and a button straight to the trunk.
  5. You get an email back when someone presses Looks Good or Needs a Change. Make any change on the list and press Send Again.
  6. Print the packing list with Packing List PDF, or choose Save as PDF in the print window. It has a box to tick for every line and lines to sign.

Emails You Get

  • New Speakers to Register · Board Members to Register · MISMO Team to Register · sponsorship invoices and payment follow-ups · The Trunk Looks Good / Needs a Change · Tasks Due This Week.
Rosalyn MillikenWorks with the hotel: the resume, room sets, furniture, food and beverage, and arrival and departure dates.
Your pages

What You Do

  1. Open Hotel Specs and pick a day. The rooms show how each is set, what is in it from morning to evening, and how full it gets. Press a room to see its week.
  2. Check the food and beverage for the day in the order it happens. Press a meal or break to see its sponsor and headcount and paste in its menu; it goes straight onto the Resume. Lunch is only ever the Newcomer Orientation; everyone else is on their own.
  3. Type the headcounts in the rail on the right: General Sessions at the top, then the Newcomer Orientation, the Board and the Joint Committee. A bar shows whether the room holds them.
  4. Work the Questions for the Hotel. Move each one along with a press: To Ask, Waiting, Answered (or Not Needed). Add a new one at the bottom.
  5. Read the set-up notes under How the Rooms Are Set. A note that names a room shows on that room’s tile; press the room name to find it. Press ✓ Done once it is handled.
  6. Fill in the Resume. Fill Next takes you to the next detail still TBD. Open a function to see it exactly as it prints beside its fields.
  7. Fill in your travel form when it arrives, so you are on the rooming list.

Emails You Get

  • New Summit Sponsor · Tasks Due This Week · the MISMO team travel form.

04The Left Menu
  • Search finds a session, a task or a person wherever it lives and takes you to it.
  • The pages, in three groups: The Plan (Run of Show, Schedule, General Sessions, Workshop), The People (People, Registration) and The Hotel (Hotel Specs, Resume, The Trunk). Each has its own section below.
  • Summit picks which Summit every tab is showing. The 2027 Summits are Winter (InterContinental New Orleans), Spring (Salt Lake Marriott Downtown at City Creek) and Fall (The Bethesdan, Bethesda).
  • Undo steps back the last change, on any tab. Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) does the same.
  • Backup downloads everything Summit HQ holds as one file, or puts a backup file back.
  • System Health shows whether saving, storage and the email flows are working. Its dot is green when all is well, amber for a warning and red when something needs attention; red also puts a bar across the top of the page for everyone.
  • Help is this page.
  • Sponsorship Portal is the stamp that says when Summit HQ last checked the portal. ✓ 0 new changes means the two are in step. N new changes, not copied yet means the portal has saved something Summit HQ does not have yet; it normally clears within minutes. Last copy is when the portal’s information last arrived. It checks when the page opens and every 30 minutes.
  • Dark Mode switches the colors. The arrow at the top (or the backslash key) narrows the menu to icons.
05Run of Show: The Work and the Deadlines

Run of Show is the task list for the whole Summit cycle. The strip across the top switches between its views.

The Countdown at the Top

  • A live countdown to 8:00 AM on the Summit’s first day, ticking by the second.
  • Next Up is the earliest open task with a date (anything overdue shows first, in red). Click it to open the task.
  • The ring shows how much of this cycle’s plan is complete; the red slice is what is overdue.
  • The Road to the Summit places every dated task on one line from the start of the cycle to three weeks after the Summit, colored by status, with milestones as diamonds and a marker for today. Hover a dot to see the task; click it to open it.
  • The figures under it (Overdue, Due Next 14 Days, To Discuss, In Progress, Complete) each open the list behind them.

Finding Your Way

  • The menu on the left reads in three groups: The Plan (Run of Show, Schedule, General Sessions, Workshop), The People (People, Registration) and The Hotel (Hotel Specs, Resume, The Trunk). People, Hotel Specs and The Trunk are pages of their own.
  • People opens on the Confirmed Speakers face by face, each ringed by how far along they are, with the next step under their name and the five steps as bars underneath. Click a face to open that speaker.
  • General Sessions shows The Lineup under The Day: every session as a card with its time, who is on (their headshots) and its sponsor. Click a card to go to it.
  • On the Schedule, hover anywhere on the week and its room and its time light up; type in Find on the Grid and everything else dims. The week always fits the window, so the grid itself never scrolls up and down. Enlarge opens the week full screen with taller rows; drag and click work the same, and Close or Esc puts it back.

Opening a task, an agenda item or a session. It opens wide on the right, laid out like the Certification Management panel. The navy top has its name and a few tags (phase, scope, day, room, status). Under it, numbered steps show where it stands; press one to move it there. The box under the steps says what to do next, with the buttons to do it. Then come the tabs. Overview has the record at a glance (owner, due date, room, headcount, chairs and so on) and its notes; type or pick straight in those boxes and it saves when you click away, and the same field on Details follows along. Details has every field to edit. Notes (tasks and agenda items) is the running log, and Conflicts (sessions) lists anything that clashes. The tab you were last on comes back next time.

Save. A task, an agenda item, a Resume section or a person opened on the right has a Save button at the bottom whenever there is something to type in. Everything is written as you go; Save makes sure the field you are in is written too, and closes the panel. Close a panel after changing something without pressing Save and it asks first: Save Changes, Discard Changes (puts back what each box said when you opened it) or Keep Editing.

The Buttons Above the Calendar

The Plan, Planning Meeting and All Tasks switch the view without moving you back to the top of the page. + New Task adds a task. + Add A Summit opens the panel where you name a new Summit and drop its hotel contract in; the Schedule, the cycle, the Contract viewer and the resume are written together.

Past Summits

  • Every summit you plan here is kept. Pick it in the Summit picker and the Schedule (sessions, attendance, AV, chairs, who is leading each one), the Resume, Hotel Specs, People and speaker steps, the Board of Directors card (with that summit’s Board), MISMO Team travel, the Trunk, Registration and Sponsors show what they were for that summit.
  • The Run of Show is one running plan, so about 10 days after a summit starts its tasks, Planning Meeting agenda and Meeting Notes are kept as they stood. Past Summits on the Schedule Timeline opens any summit’s kept plan, read only. Picking a summit that is over on the Schedule Timeline no longer moves the Run of Show back to it.
  • Session details you change (attendance, AV, chairs, leaders, times, a session taken off) belong to the summit picked when you change them; the session’s name and description are shared, so a fix there shows everywhere. A session you add belongs to that summit and the ones after it.
  • A person’s bio, title and headshot are the latest ones on file, not the ones from an earlier summit.

The Plan

  • The calendar runs the full width of the page with every task on its due date. Drag a task to another day to move it. To move it into another month, hold it over the ‹ or › arrows and the calendar turns the page. Click a task to open it.
  • Needs a Date, under the calendar, holds every open task with no date. Drag one onto a day to give it a date, or drag a dated task there to take its date off.
  • Meeting Notes run across the page under the calendar. + New Note adds one, → Task turns it into a task, and a note grows to fit what is typed in it.

Planning Meeting

The whole meeting on one board, in the order it runs. Every task appears on it once: a question about a task rides on that task’s card, a task already being talked about is not listed again further down, and a finished task with an old flag is not raised again.

  • The top says what there is to cover and has four numbered steps; click one to jump to it. The bar fills as things are decided.
  • Talk About Today has three lanes. Carried Over is anything still Being Discussed. New to Raise is anything flagged or set to Need to Discuss, plus agenda items. Type in Add something to raise to add an agenda item. Drag a card between lanes as the conversation moves; drag it into Decided once it is settled (a task goes back to In Progress and its questions close).
  • Fix Before It Slips lists open tasks that are overdue, have no date or have no owner. Pick an owner or a date right on the line, or press Done; the line drops off once it is fixed.
  • Coming Up shows the next six weeks, a week to a column, with the Schedule milestones and the Summit itself marked. The bar on each week shows how much of it is done. Drag a task to another week to move it; it keeps its weekday. Any task on the board, in any lane, can be moved this way: the moment you pick one up, a strip of weeks rises from the bottom of the screen, out to Summit week, so you can drop it on a week without scrolling. Who Is Carrying These Six Weeks shows each person’s load (click a name for their tasks), and See the Whole Run opens the full countdown from 20+ weeks out to after the Summit.
  • Marked To Automate lists tasks that should stop being done by hand, across every Summit. Drag a task onto it to mark it.
  • The Schedule box shows this Summit’s two scheduling milestones (the Chair Survey 104 days out and the finalized schedule 97 days out, each on a Tuesday) and whether they are done. Every Summit’s Timeline opens the list for every Summit, where a Summit can also be added by name and first day.

All Tasks

Every task, to sort and filter. + New Task adds one. A task has an owner, people who assist, a due date, a status (Not Started, In Progress, Need to Discuss, Being Discussed, Complete), a description and notes. Tasks marked All Summits come back every cycle; This Summit Only tasks do not.

06Schedule: The Week Room by Room

The Schedule (the color grid) places every workgroup meeting, session, meal and reception in a room and a time for each day of the Summit. Everything else reads from it: Hotel Specs, the resume, the event app’s sessions file and the printed schedule.

  • Drag a session to move it to another room or time. Locked sessions stay where they are.
  • Each room shows its capacity from the hotel contract, so a session too big for its room stands out.
  • Arrangement Options builds a clean week that respects every request and keeps sessions that should not overlap apart.
  • Held for Next Summit keeps a note about a future Summit (“these two should never run together”) without changing the week in front of you.
  • Rooms change every Summit. Add A Summit makes the first pass from the hotel contract, and the Rooms card lets you add, rename, remove or update a room, the days it is held and what it is used for (Workgroup, General Sessions, Breakfast, Staff Office and so on).
  • Fixed lists the set pieces of the week: Breakfast, the Staff Office, Champions Lounge, Member Engagement, Newcomer Orientation, the Workshop, both Receptions, General Sessions and the Joint Committee Meeting. Each one shows the room it sits in on the grid. The first time, it goes in the room whose use matches (Breakfast for the receptions, General Sessions for the Joint Committee); drag the card on the grid to change it. A line turns red if it has no room, or if the General Sessions room seats fewer in classroom than the headcount.
  • The floor plan, capacity chart and contract for each Summit open from the Schedule.
  • Facilitator choices on each session come from the MMS (People and Roles › Facilitators), so a facilitator added or removed there shows here too. Walk-on types a name for this Summit only, and TBD holds the spot.
  • Chair Survey prepares the survey to workgroup chairs that informs the grid. Print / PDF prints the week.

General Sessions on Tuesday sit at the top of the grid in the main ballroom. MISMO Link Office Hours and the Champions Lounge are in separate rooms.

07Hotel Specs: What the Hotel Sets Up

Everything the hotel sets up, room by room and day by day, read from the Schedule. Nothing here is typed twice: the same numbers and notes feed the Resume.

Ready for the Hotel

The ring at the top shows how ready the page is, with a bar for each part: headcounts in, meals and breaks with a menu, and questions for the hotel answered. Press a line and the page takes you to where it is filled in; Menus Set goes to the first day with a meal still missing its menu.

Pick a Day

Monday to Thursday, each with how many rooms are in use and the biggest crowd that day. Everything under it follows the day you pick.

Food & Beverage

  • The day’s breakfast, breaks, the Newcomer Orientation lunch and the receptions, in the order they happen, each with the expected crowd, the sponsor and whether the menu is set. A break with a big crowd says what it needs (food as well as coffee, or two stations).
  • There is no lunch for anyone but the Newcomer Orientation; everyone else is on their own at midday.
  • Press one and a small window opens for just that meal or break: whether it has a sponsor, how many are coming (each dot is about 10 people), and a box to paste the menu into. The menu saves as you paste and prints on the Resume under that function.
  • Sponsors fill in from the Sponsorship Portal once a sponsorship is approved and has its day set; anything sold without a day is listed so it can be set there.

The Rooms

  • Every meeting room is a tile: its set-up drawn from above (U, classroom, theater, rounds and so on), what is in it morning to evening, and a bar for how full it gets (green fits, amber is close, red is over).
  • A set-up note that names the room shows on its tile.
  • Press a room to see its whole week and its set-up notes; Open the Schedule to move things.

Numbers & Notes for the Hotel (the column on the right)

  • General Sessions Headcount drives Tuesday, the room check and most of the catering. Type it in the box; the bar shows the seats against the room.
  • Headcounts for the Newcomer Orientation, the Board and the Joint Committee are typed right there; last summit’s number shows faintly until you do. The Board’s comes in on its own from the In Person count on People.
  • Questions for the Hotel: move each one along with a press, To Ask, Waiting, Answered, or mark it Not Needed. Answered ones fold away underneath. Press the words to change them; add a new question at the bottom.
  • How the Rooms Are Set holds Rosalyn’s set-up notes. A note that names a room carries that room’s name; press it to find the room. Press ✓ Done when a note is taken care of; it folds away under Done, where Reopen puts it back. Add a new note at the bottom.
  • Full List on any of them opens everything in that list to edit, including the menus, notes for Rosalyn and which list a line belongs in.
  • Contract, Floor Plan & Capacities opens the hotel contract and floor plans.
08General Sessions: Tuesday’s Running Order

The Day, under the figures, draws the whole General Sessions as one ribbon from the start time to the end time: each segment is as wide as it runs, breaks and lunch are striped, sponsored segments carry a gold edge, and anything past the end time turns red. Click a segment to jump to it.

Builds Tuesday’s General Sessions segment by segment for the Summit picked in the left menu.

  • Start from the Typical Tuesday template, or Start Blank. Start Over clears it.
  • Add a segment, give it a type (fireside chat, case study, presentation, panel, lunch and so on), a title, a description and a length. Drag segments to reorder them, or use the arrows. The times recalculate from the start time; pin a time when a segment must start at a set time and any gap or clash is flagged.
  • Drag names from the Presenters list on the right onto a segment to add them, then choose their role: Speaker, Moderator, Panelist or Host. The list can show this Summit’s people, those not placed yet, lenders, or everyone.
  • Lenders are highlighted. A presenter whose company is a lender in Member 360 (Member Type Lender, or the Lender/Servicer sector) is marked automatically. The company name on their People record is matched to Member 360; when Member 360 has that exact company as a non-lender (First American, the title company, say), they are not marked, even if a similarly named bank is a lender. A name Member 360 does not have exactly is matched to the closest lender name that starts the same way. To correct anyone, click the Lender or L? mark on their chip; that choice is kept for this Summit. The tiles at the top count segments with a lender, and presenters still missing a bio or headshot.
  • Print Agenda prints the running order. The segments also go into the event app’s sessions file in place of a single General Sessions block.
  • Show on the Website Agenda lets the website’s agenda show this running order: each segment’s time, title, description and sponsor, and each speaker’s name, title, company and headshot (never an email or a note). It is off until you turn it on, one summit at a time, for General Sessions and the Workshop each. Changes made afterwards reach the website on their own. Click it again to take the running order off.

The Workshop

Workshop in the left menu works exactly the same way for Monday afternoon’s Workshop. Start from a Typical Workshop (a welcome, sections, a break, a hands-on exercise and a wrap-up) or start blank, add sections, and drag speakers onto them from the Confirmed Speakers list on the right. Its start and end times come from the Workshop on the Schedule. Each Summit keeps its own Workshop, and its sections go into the event app’s sessions file in place of the single Workshop block. A speaker put on a section shows it under Sessions They Are In on People, and the speaker email names it.

09Resume: What the Hotel Receives

The resume is the document the hotel works from. It is never edited in Word: everything in it comes from the Schedule, Hotel Specs, and the fields on this tab (rates, room block, cutoff, VIPs, staff, rooming).

  • Issue a version when it is ready to send. Each version is numbered and dated.
  • The Word document shows every difference from the version before as a tracked change, so the hotel sees exactly what moved. The Final PDF is the clean copy for the hotel and for on-site.
  • Versions & Changes lists every version issued and what is waiting to go into the next one.
  • The page at the top shows how ready the resume is, every section as a tile (green complete, amber still TBD, blue changed since the last version) and each day’s functions. Fill Next takes you to the next detail still TBD.
  • Every Section, in the Order It Prints: each section is a card with its status. Open one to fill it in. Schedule changes not yet on the resume show as an amber banner above them.
  • A function, opened under Functions, Day by Day, shows As It Prints beside its fields and redraws as you type. The suggestions under a part are lines the other functions use; press one to add it. A part you have typed over is marked Edited, with a link to go back to the Schedule’s wording.
10The Trunk: Packing and Review

Bernie’s packing list and the trunk, side by side. The Standard Kit and the ribbons are the same every Summit; sponsor merch and what is packed are per Summit, so the trunk starts empty for the next one.

  • The road across the top shows the Packing List task (with how much is in the trunk), the Team Review, and the trunk shipping, each with its due date and how many days are left. Press a task to open it.
  • Pack a line by dragging it into the trunk, or with its Pack button. On a phone, press and hold a line for a moment to pick it up. A tap never moves anything.
  • Amounts and names are changed right on the packing list: the − and + buttons set how many, and the item and note are typed straight in. Add something to pack at the foot of the list adds a new line to whichever list you pick. Sponsor Merch can bring in this Summit’s sponsors in one press.
  • A packed line is pressed to change it, take it out or delete it.
  • Send for Review emails the team you pick (Jonna, Amy and Kelly to start) with the packing list and a button straight to the trunk. There they press Looks Good or Needs a Change, and Bernie is emailed either way. Change the list after it has gone out and it says so, with Send Again.
  • Packing List PDF makes a branded, printable packing list with a box to tick for every line; choose Save as PDF in the print window to download it.
  • When the last line goes in, the lid comes down: Packed and Ready to Ship.

Bernie’s steps, one by one, are under Your Part, Person by Person.

11Registration: The Weekly Numbers

The weekly registration report for the Summit picked, compared with last year at the same week. Week 0 is the Friday before the Summit opens.

  • The numbers update themselves every Friday. At 6 AM Eastern, Reporting Services emails that week’s registrations from Aptify (the report SummitHQ_Registration in the Mismo folder on reports.mba.org) to mismosummit@mba.org, with Jonna copied. The Summit HQ - Registration Weekly Pull flow saves it, and the first time anyone opens Summit HQ afterward, Registration takes in this year’s registrants (in person and virtual), last year’s for the same summit, and that Friday’s row on Week-by-Week History. A company keeps the category it was given before; a new one gets one from its Aptify company type. Sponsorships carry over from the last week that had them. Nobody uploads anything.
  • Update the Numbers still loads files by hand (Vanessa’s dashboard exports), and Week-by-Week History takes a Friday’s numbers typed in. Whichever came in last stands.
  • Registrations come from the Aptify view Event Attendance w/ Prompt, run with the Summit’s name so it counts in-person and virtual. Sponsorship dollars come from the Sponsorship Portal’s Money tab.
  • Each week is kept as it was reported. Cancelled orders drop out of Aptify, so rebuilding an old week from today’s export can come out lower.
  • The bottom of the tab explains exactly how each number is counted.
  • Weekly List to Sponsors. The card under the registrant lists shows when the Friday list to sponsors goes (12:00 PM Eastern, from week 7 through the Friday before the Summit), the email’s wording and a preview. Kelly (or anyone who edits Summit HQ) can change the subject and message and press Save; the next Friday’s email uses it. Fill-ins: {summit}, {opens}, {count} and {asof}. Send a Test to Me sends it to you only, marked [Test]. Kelly’s signature and the line about email addresses are always added.
  • Sent lists every Friday that went: when, how many sponsors and registrants, and the subject. Click one to see who got it (company, contact and email), the email exactly as it went, and the list that was attached. This is the record instead of copying Jonna and Kelly.
12Speakers, Sponsors and the Board, Start to Finish

The People Page

  • The dark band and the speaker faces stay at the top. Click a tile (Bios in Hand, Registered, On the Event App, Board Registered) or one of the five step bars to list just the people behind it; click a face to open that speaker on the right.
  • The list comes a page at a time, 20 to start. Per Page under the list changes it to 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 or All (remembered in this browser), and Back and Next move through the pages. Changing the filter or the search starts again at page 1.
  • The same person twice? Open the one to keep. If another record has the same email, or the same first name at the same company, a note at the top says so; Same Person Twice? on the right lists them, or finds any other record by name, email or company. Merge Into This One (click twice) keeps the open record, fills in anything it is missing from the other one (email, title, bio, headshot, the fuller name), puts together their progress on every summit (sessions, steps done, the latest invitation), and retires the other record. Undo puts both back. Nothing is emailed.
  • One list of everyone at this summit, one row a person whatever their roles: a speaker who is also on the MISMO Team is one row. The boxes on top are the lists behind them: click Need Something From Us, Speakers, Board of Directors, MISMO Team, Sponsors, Speaker Prospects or Master List of Speakers to show just those people. Someone on the master list who is not on this summit opens the same way, with + Speaker on This Summit and + Speaker Prospect. The search also looks through the master list.
  • Click anyone and everything about them opens on the right, in the same panel as everywhere else (the expand button makes it wide, with two columns): the one next thing and whose it is; their contact details; the headshot and bio side by side (drop a photo on the headshot, or their Word, PDF or text bio file on the bio, and its words go in ready to edit); then a section for each role they hold: Speaker (the speaker email, the form link, weekly follow-ups, the five steps and their sessions), MISMO Team (arrives, departs, group, parking, the travel form and Bernie), Board of Directors (in person, virtually or not attending, the ask and Bernie), Sponsor (from the portal, with the agenda mark) and Speaker Prospect; then the note for this summit and their history. Every change saves as you go.
  • Hotel Nights shows the MISMO Team’s stays as one bar a person with the rooms each night, and anything to check before it goes to the hotel.
  • Emails & Asks, Full Lists, Downloads and + Add a Person open the very same tools as the cards (Choose Speakers to Email, the Board ask, Notify Bernie, the travel ask, the full Board and Team lists, the speakers and sessions files). Every email still opens its preview first; nothing goes out until you press Send.

A Speaker

  1. Placed on a Session. Amy places the speaker on their General Sessions segment or Workshop section, and the agenda builds itself from there, so this ticks itself once they are on a session. Jonna ticks it only for someone on the agenda some other way.
  2. Asked for a bio and headshot (Amy).
  3. Bio and headshot in hand (Amy). Ticks itself once both are in.
  4. Registered for the event (Bernie).
  5. On the event app (Vanessa). The bio and the headshot each get their own tick.

Adding a speaker on People puts them on Bernie’s next New Speakers to Register email on its own; he gets one list each weekday morning, not an email per speaker.

A Sponsor

  1. The sponsor applies on the Prospectus, and the team works it in the Sponsorship Portal through approval and payment.
  2. Approved sponsors appear on the Sponsors From The Portal card on their own, with their status (Approved, Pending Payment or Paid), level, what they are sponsoring, and their comp code and number of comps. They register themselves with the code, so sponsors are never registered from Summit HQ.
  3. Once approved, the website’s Summit Sponsor Feed puts them on the website agenda by itself, within the hour on weekdays.
  4. On the event app (Vanessa). Downloads → Sponsors File lists every approved sponsor with their level, what they sponsor, website and logo; she presses Mark On the Event App on each once they are in. Until then their Next Step reads Vanessa: Put them on the event app.
  5. Breakfasts, breaks and receptions they sponsor show on Hotel Specs automatically once the day is set in the portal.

The People Tab Tools

Each of these opens on the right from Full Lists, Emails & Asks or + Add a Person at the top of People, or from a person’s own panel.

  • Confirmed Speakers lists this Summit’s speakers.
  • Speaker Prospects is who you might ask to speak. Mark each one Invited, Accepted or Declined. Accepted makes them a Confirmed Speaker; Declined keeps them on the list for future Summits. Edit on a row opens their name, email, title and company to change right there, with a Notes for This Summit box (who suggested them, the topic, when to follow up).
  • Sessions They Are In on a speaker’s row puts them on that General Sessions segment or Workshop section too.
  • Master List of Speakers is everyone who has spoken or been added before. The search box at the top of the list narrows it as you type (a name, company, title or email). Press + Add as Speaker to put someone on this Summit.
  • The speaker email. Send Speaker Email on a speaker opens the email to check and send. This Email changes just this one; Template for Every Speaker changes the wording for everyone on this Summit. Add a Link under the message puts in a link: type the words to show and the web address (or select words first). Tick Show as a button to make it a navy button on a line of its own, the way the Send My Bio & Headshot button looks; in the message box a button reads as the words in double square brackets followed by the link. A web address typed on its own is a link too. These fill in for each speaker: {first}, {session}, {sessionDate}, {summitShort}, {dates}, {gsDate}; from the Resume, {roomBlock} (the web address in Reservations under Event Details; it can sit beside the phone number) and {rate} (the dollar amount in Group Guestroom Rate under Accommodations); and {infoLink}, the speaker’s own link to send their bio and headshot. If the Resume does not have the booking link or the rate yet, the email says so in yellow and shows a reminder in its place.
  • Bio and headshot, collected for you. The speaker email carries each speaker’s own link to a short MISMO form (resources.mismo.org/summit-hq/speaker.html): their bio, title, company, LinkedIn and a headshot, which the form makes the right size on their side. Instead of pasting their bio, they can drop it in as a Word, PDF or text file; the form puts the words in the bio box for them to check and sends the file too. On their record in People, Their bio file shows under the Bio with Review the File, which opens the words to read and copy (Copy All, or select any part), Use This as Their Bio, the PDF itself when it is one, and Download the File. Copy the Bio copies whatever is in their Bio box. Sending the email ticks Asked for bio & headshot. What they send lands on their row within a few minutes of People being open: the bio, title, company and headshot fill in, and Bio & headshot in hand ticks itself. The Bio & Headshot Form line on their row says whether the link went out and when they answered; Copy Their Link gives you their link to paste into an email of your own. They can use the same link again to change anything.
  • Speaker Emails & Follow-Ups is its own card on People. The tiles show how many speakers have been emailed, who is still waiting on a bio or headshot, the next follow-up and who is all in. Under them, every speaker has one line: whether their bio and headshot are in, their next follow-up, and their own On/Off switch.
    • Choose Speakers to Email opens the email with a list of speakers to tick. Switch between Not Emailed Yet, Waiting on Bio or Headshot and Everyone, search for a name, or use Pick All Shown and Clear. Only the ones ticked get it, each filled in for them; press Preview to see anyone’s copy. Speaker Email and Reminder at the top switch which email you are sending.
    • The speaker email goes out on its own. With Send Automatically on, a confirmed speaker’s email goes out by itself ten minutes after they are placed in a session (from Sessions They Are In on People, or by dragging them onto General Sessions or the Workshop). The ten minutes are there so a slip can be undone; their line on the card shows the time it will go, with Send Now and Hold. It uses the Template for Every Speaker and needs an email address on their record. Speakers who were already in a session when this was switched on (November 4, 2026) are not sent anything on their own: send theirs from Choose Speakers to Email. Summit HQ sends it the next time anyone has People open, so it can wait until someone opens Summit HQ.
    • Someone who should not get the speaker email (their sponsor or an assistant is sending the bio and headshot, say): turn off Send Them the Speaker Email on their record, or their switch on the Speaker Emails & Follow-Ups card. Nothing goes to them on its own, they are left out of Not Emailed Yet, and no reminders start. Copy Their Link on their record gives you their bio and headshot form link to pass to whoever is sending it.
    • Returning speakers. A speaker who has spoken at an earlier Summit and whose bio and headshot are already on file is told so in their email and asked only whether they want to send an updated one; they get no reminders. In the Template for Every Speaker, a paragraph that starts [New speakers] goes only to everyone else, and one that starts [Returning speakers] goes only to them. {lastSummit} fills in the last Summit they spoke at.
    • Bio and headshot by email. When a speaker emails their headshot or bio instead of using the form, you do not need to put it in. Jonna is copied on every speaker email, and a flow watches her inbox: an email with attachments from a speaker’s address goes straight onto their record — the biggest photo becomes their headshot, and a Word, PDF or text file becomes their bio file, with its words put in as their bio. If it came only to Amy, forward it to Jonna (keep their email address in what you forward) and it is matched the same way. It shows on their line as Emailed with the day, and the follow-ups stop once both are in. If they already had a headshot or bio, the new one waits on their row under Came by Email: Use the New Headshot, Use the New Bio, or Keep What We Have. A bio typed into the body of an email still needs copying in by hand.
    • Each Summit has its own speaker email. A Summit whose speaker email has not been saved yet starts from the last Summit’s saved wording, not the original standard one: its dates move to the new Summit, and the hotel, workshop name and reception sponsor are swapped in. A yellow note on Template for Every Speaker says so; read it through for anything that was only for the last Summit (a room name, say) and press Save for Every Speaker. Until it is saved for that Summit, speaker emails there do not go out on their own. The Board, the MISMO Team, the follow-ups and the bio and headshot answers are kept per Summit too, and the MISMO Team list starts from the last Summit’s people without their dates.
    • Saving your changes. In a speaker’s email, Save sits at the top. On This Email it keeps your changes for that one speaker: their own saved email is what goes to them, whether you send it or it goes on its own, and Go Back to the Template Wording drops it. On Template for Every Speaker, Save for Every Speaker saves the wording everyone gets and checks the saved copy before it says Saved ✓. Until you save, it says Changes not saved yet, and closing asks whether to save. Changes typed in Choose Speakers to Email go in those emails only and do not change the template.
    • Send a Test to Me, beside the send button on any speaker email or reminder, sends that exact email to you only, from Amy and marked [Test], so you can check it in your inbox. Its bio and headshot button goes to a practice copy of the form, so trying it does not change the speaker’s record.
    • Weekly follow-ups happen on their own. Sending a speaker their email marks the day. From then on, anyone who still owes a bio or headshot gets a reminder every week on that same day of the week, until their bio and headshot are in or the Summit starts. The reminder says exactly what is still missing (bio, headshot, or both) and has the Send My Bio & Headshot button. The Summit HQ - Speaker Reminders flow sends them each morning at 7:17 AM Mountain, skips anyone who has already sent theirs through the form, and never sends the same one twice.
    • Turning them off. The Weekly Follow-Ups switch at the top turns them off for the whole Summit; each speaker’s own switch turns them off for just that person. Turn either back on and they pick up again.
    • Every speaker email and every reminder goes out from Amy (amoses@mismo.org, through Jonna’s Outlook, which has Send As for Amy’s mailbox). Amy and Jonna are copied, and replies go to Amy.
  • Ask In Person or Virtual on the Board of Directors card emails board members a branded note from Jonna: their registration is complimentary, and two buttons, In Person and Virtually (with a link for not able to attend). They confirm on a short MISMO page, and their answer marks them on the card by itself, with any note they add. Pick who gets it (No Answer Yet or Everyone), preview each one, and use Send a Test to Me first. Tim Bowler’s, Michele Bodda’s and Peter Grace’s emails copy the assistants who do their scheduling. The email gives the Board meeting’s day, hours and room from the Schedule. Alexandra Brinton and Michael Briggs from MBA are asked too (their email says their registration is complimentary as part of the Board meeting); Brian Vieaux and MISMO staff are not.
  • Board of Directors lists the Board from the MISMO Leadership page. Mark each person In Person, Virtual or Not Attending (or let their answer to the email do it); the tally at the top keeps count, and the In Person number becomes the Board of Directors headcount on Hotel Specs so Rosalyn orders the right amount of food. Press Registered once Bernie has registered someone. Check the box at the start of each board member’s row that Bernie should register, then press Notify Bernie (it shows how many are checked; click it twice to send). Everyone who answered In Person or Virtual and is not registered or sent to him yet starts checked; Check Everyone Ready and Clear sit beside the button. He gets one email with the people you ticked, within about 20 minutes, and each row shows when they were sent to him.
  • MISMO Team at the Summit is everyone going under the MISMO banner: staff, Ros and Bernie, the facilitators, the architect, and guests added if there is room. Everyone on the list is going; what the card collects is their arrival and departure, for the hotel. Ask for Travel Dates opens the email first: pick who gets it (Not Asked Yet, Waiting on Form or Everyone), preview each one, use Send a Test to Me, and only then send. Each gets a branded email from you with their own link to enter when they arrive and leave and, when the hotel includes it, whether they need parking. Their answers fill in their row, the Rooms by night count (what to tell the hotel) and, on their own, the Resume’s Guestroom and Rate Assignments: everyone with dates is added there with their Arrives – Departs. To send people to Bernie, check the box at the start of their row (everyone with dates not yet sent to him starts checked) and press Send to Bernie; you and Amy are copied. The team is never on Bernie’s speaker list. Each Summit keeps its own list; a new Summit starts from the last one’s team (names, emails and groups, without guests or dates), so you only add or take off who changed.
  • Speakers file and Sessions file download the event app’s upload files, column for column, ready for Vanessa.
13How the Systems Connect
  • Sponsorship Portal → Summit HQ. Every time the portal saves, the Sponsorship Team Emails flow in Power Automate wakes within seconds. It sends the portal’s emails, updates the Sponsorship Requests list, and copies the portal’s sponsorships into Summit HQ. That copy feeds People (paid sponsors, comp codes) and Hotel Specs (food and break sponsors). The stamp in the left menu shows whether the copy is current.
  • Member 360 → General Sessions. Member 360’s list of organizations says which are lenders, so General Sessions can highlight lender presenters.
  • Summit HQ → the event app. The speakers and sessions files from People are uploaded to the event app by Vanessa.
  • Summit HQ → the hotel. The resume, issued from the Resume tab.
  • Summit HQ → the scheduled emails. Summit HQ keeps two small ready-to-read summaries up to date on its own whenever anything changes: the open tasks (read by the Monday task email) and each Summit’s registrants by company, name, job title and In-Person or Virtual (read by the Registration List to Sponsors email, together with that email’s finished wording). That flow writes back what it sent each Friday, which Registration shows under Weekly List to Sponsors.
  • People → Bernie. Each speaker added on People is written to a small ready-made list that the New Speakers to Register flow reads every weekday morning, so Bernie gets one email rather than one per speaker.
  • Aptify → Registration. The SummitHQ_Registration report is emailed every Friday morning and Summit HQ loads it by itself (see Registration). Files from Vanessa’s dashboard can still be loaded by hand.

15Backups, Undo and History
  • Undo takes back the last change on any tab, one step at a time.
  • Backup → Download saves everything (tasks, schedule, people and headshots, resume versions, registration) as one file. Do it monthly and before any big change. Backup → Restore writes a backup file back in. An empty Summit HQ offers to restore on its own.
  • Every save is recorded in the data repository, so Perry can recover an earlier version of anything even without a backup.
  • Every resume version ever issued is kept on the Resume tab.
16Changing the Page Itself

Day-to-day work never needs this: tasks, sessions, people and the resume are all changed in the page. This is only for changing how Summit HQ itself works or looks.

  1. Go to github.com/GitMISMO/summit-hq and download the current index.html. Always start from the copy on GitHub; an older copy would undo recent changes.
  2. Make the change. Keep the sign-in block at the very top of the file.
  3. On the repository page choose Add file → Upload files, drop in the new index.html, write a short note of what changed, and press Commit changes.
  4. GitHub runs Summit HQ’s checks, and only when they pass does it go live on resources.mismo.org, about 4 minutes after the upload. Reload Summit HQ to see it. If a check fails, the page stays as it was and GitHub emails you which check failed.

Two helpers live in the lib folder beside index.html and load only when they are used: docx.js writes the resume as a Word file, and pdfjs-lib.js with pdfjs-worker.js read a hotel contract PDF in Add A Summit. Leave that folder in place; without it those two buttons stop working.

Each part of Summit HQ waits until its own information has loaded before it saves anything, so a slow connection can never write a blank copy over real work. If a save is tried too early it says Still loading; try again a moment later.

Automatic checks. Every upload to GitHub runs Summit HQ’s checks (the tests folder) before it goes live: every tab opens, saving and merging work, each summit keeps its own details, Past Summits, the Board and Team emails, System Health, and files sent in from outside can never run inside the page. If any check fails, the change does not go live, GitHub emails whoever uploaded, and the repository’s Actions tab says which one. In an emergency only, a change can go live without the checks: Actions → Summit HQ Checks and Publish → Run workflow, tick Skip the checks.

Never put names, emails, contracts or other private details in the page; they belong in the saved information, which only arrives after sign-in. If a change breaks the page, open index.html’s history on GitHub and put the previous version back the same way.

17When Something Goes Wrong
What You SeeWhat to Do
A red bar across the top, or a red dot on System HealthPress Details. It names what stopped: a flow (open that flow in Power Automate, check its run history, resubmit a failed run and sign in any connection showing an error; turn it back on if it was turned off), saving (keep the tab open; tell Perry if it does not clear) or storage (tell Perry before the file is full). Copy Report copies everything it found, ready to paste into an email.
Something looks broken but there is no red barOpen System Health. Team Error Log lists the errors anyone’s Summit HQ has hit in the last 7 days, with who and which tab, so the problem can be found without asking around.
The page keeps asking you to sign in, or shows nothingSign out and back in. If it still will not open, ask Perry to check your Summit HQ access.
Your change does not show for someone elseWait 30 seconds and have them reload. If the page says a save failed, reload and make the change again. If saves keep failing, the save relay may be down: tell Perry.
The portal stamp says changes are not copied, for more than a dayOpen the Sponsorship Team Emails flow in Power Automate and check its run history. Resubmit a failed run; if its connections show an error, sign them in again.
A food or break sponsor is missing from Hotel SpecsIn the Sponsorship Portal, check the sponsorship is approved and has its day set. Sponsorships with no day are listed in the note on Hotel Specs.
A speaker was not on Bernie’s morning listCheck the speaker is on this Summit in People and not already marked Registered (registered speakers drop off). Then open Summit HQ - New Speakers to Register in Power Automate and look at the morning’s run. It only runs on weekdays.
Bernie did not get the board emailIt goes 5 to 20 minutes after Notify Bernie is pressed. If it still has not come, check the Summit HQ - Board Members to Register flow’s run history.
The Monday email is missing or looks wrongCheck the Summit HQ - Monday Task Email flow’s run history. It reads Summit HQ’s tasks as of the last change anyone made, so fixing a task in Run of Show fixes the next email.
Something was deleted or changed by mistakePress Undo. If it is too late for Undo, restore from the latest backup, or ask Perry to recover it from the saved history.
The page broke after someone changed itOn GitHub, put the previous index.html back (see Changing the Page Itself).
18Limits and Known Gaps
The flows and the Summit HQ People list belong to Jonna’s account. Until a co-owner is added and the list is moved, they would stop if that account were closed.
  • Nothing adds speakers to the Summit HQ People list automatically, so Bernie’s email only goes when someone adds them there.
  • The Sponsorship Portal copy only refreshes when the portal saves. If the portal is quiet, the stamp still shows when Summit HQ last checked.
  • Sponsors register themselves with their comp code; Summit HQ does not track their registration.
